Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * Duo lead times extend to Jan 2027; US carrier availability better at 50 days versus 102 days on Apple's website.
  * iPhone 18 Pro lead times declined slightly to 8 days (vs 9 days last week); Pro Max stable at 15 days
  * China Pro lead times fell to 4 days from 11 days last week; Duo's launch day inventory is sold out globally

  
---  
| FULL REPORT|     |   
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
iPhone Duo lead times elongated, slip to Jan 2027

Our tracking of iPhone ship dates on Apple's own website, and various carrier
websites, indicates that as of Oct 19th, the global average ship time (in
days) for the iPhone Duo stands at 82 days. Fig 1 shows ship dates for the
iPhone Duo and 18 series versus prior years. Duo's availability on US carrier
websites (50 days on average) appears to be much better than Apple's own
website (102 days across all storage configurations and colors), which could
be due to varying allocations of inventory. International availability is
currently pushed out to Jan 22nd (lead time of 95 days). Reiterate Buy on
strong capital returns, eventual winner on AI at the edge and optionality from
new products/markets.

iPhone Pro declines slightly vs last week; Pro Max stable

Globally, on average, ship time for the iPhone 18 Pro is currently 8 days (vs.
9 days last week) while iPhone 18 Pro Max stands at 15 days (stable vs last
week). Compared to Week 1, iPhone 18 Pro ship dates have declined by 6 days,
while iPhone 18 Pro Max's ship dates have declined by 3 days. The Week 6 data
therefore points to continued normalization for the Pro, while Pro Max
availability remains comparatively tighter.

China: Pro declines by a week; Pro Max stable

In China, iPhone 18 Pro lead times declined to 4 days in Week 6 from 11 days
last week, indicating a meaningful improvement in availability. This is the
lowest lead time among international regions, where 18 Pro lead times
currently average at about 11 days. China's 18 Pro Max lead time was stable at
15 days and in-line with international regions. iPhone Duo lead times remain
extended at 95 days (similar to international regions).

In-store availability: Duo launch day inventory sold out

The latest in-store snapshot indicates the iPhone Duo has no in-store
availability on launch day (Oct 23rd), with Apple websites directing customers
to recheck on Oct 24th for pickup availability. Store availability remains
relatively healthy for the iPhone 18 Pro, while iPhone 18 Pro Max's
availability remains constrained. Overall, the data suggests availability
remains tighter for the Pro Max than the Pro, while initial Duo store
inventory appears to be sold out.

# Hardware & Networking

## HDD Preview: Recent Pullback Creates Positive Setup into F1Q27 as Industry
Trends Stay Intact; Favor STX vs. WDC

  
---  
  
By Joseph Cardoso
AC,
Manmohanpreet
Singh,
Marc
Vitenzon

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

We are heading into the F1Q27(Sep-end) earnings season with near-term EB,
pricing, and margin trends remaining broadly supportive of upside; however,
investor focus is increasingly shifting toward the durability of supply
discipline and overall execution, particularly in light of recent press
reports around Toshiba adding capacity and potentially acquiring TDK’s HDD
head business (see press reports
here and
here).
This is playing out against a backdrop of increasing scrutiny on the AI trade
reaching a crescendo, all of which has driven HDD shares to underperform both
our coverage universe and the broader market since the end of the summer
(average of -25% vs. -6% for Hardware & Networking and 0% for the S&P 500).

That said, we expect HDD companies to push back not only on broader concerns
around AI spending, but also on the idiosyncratic sentiment facing the sector.
We see the group as well positioned for more pronounced positives heading into
earnings season, with continued momentum around price increases driving
revenue-per-exabyte upside alongside declines in COGS-per-exabyte, supporting
continued gross margin progression for both companies. Between the two, we see
a more favorable setup for Seagate, with its leadership in the HAMR transition
creating greater scope for positive surprises in both F1Q27 results and the
F2Q27 guidance, while Western Digital’s product transitions temper near-term
results on a relative basis and place greater emphasis on the timing of
reaching parity with its peer through FY27.

While we see room for near-term upside, and for management teams to discuss
visibility into volume and pricing given LTAs while continuing to take a
disciplined approach to EB expansion via the introduction of higher-capacity
drives, supported by innovation and investments in underlying component
manufacturing, we admittedly see greater investor scrutiny around the broader
uncertainty as a tall hurdle. In our view, that likely warrants more measured
valuation multiples near-term, leading us to reset the group to mid-teens
multiples (vs. high-teens previously), which remains well ahead of the
historical multiple, supported by a robust demand and disciplined supply
environment, while still conservative relative to some other AI-levered
vendors to reflect the aggressive pricing benefits.

## Seagate (STX)

### Continued Volume and Pricing Momentum to Support Sequential Revenue and
Margin Expansion Through FY27

We expect Seagate to deliver better-than-consensus F1Q27 (Sep-end) earnings,
with both revenue and margins tracking toward the high end of the outlook,
driven by +38% y/y growth in datacenter EB shipment. Looking ahead to F2Q27
(Dec-end), we expect guidance to come in ahead of sell-side consensus,
supported by near-term upside to nearline demand on sustained cloud buildouts.
At the same time, with supply continuing to lag demand and prompting customers
to secure capacity through LTAs, we expect management to continue underscoring
extended visibility into CY28 and beyond, while also addressing the
sustainability of pricing against a backdrop of investor concern around
industry capacity additions. To that end, we are adjusting our FY27 forecast
to better reflect the ramp and transition from Mozaic 3+ to Mozaic 4+, with as
a reminder HAMR expected to account for ~50% of total nearline EB shipments by
CY26-end. However, given broader investor scrutiny around uncertainty related
to AI investments, as well as more specific risks to the HDD industry in such
an environment, particularly if additional drive capacity were to come online,
we are reducing our target multiple to the mid-teens (vs. high-teens prior),
such that our December 2027 price target now tracks to $1,050 (vs. $1,240
prior).

  * F1Q27 (Sep-end) Results: Revenue and earnings to track above the high-end of guidance and ahead of consensus driven by better-than-expected trends. We are forecasting revenue of $4.2 bn (vs. consensus of $4.1 bn and guidance of $4.0-$4.2 bn), representing growth of +62% y/y. Meanwhile, we are forecasting gross margins of 57.4% (vs. consensus of 57.4%) and operating margins of 50.3% (vs. consensus of 50.5% and guidance of ~50%), which leads to our earnings forecast of $7.58 (vs. consensus of $7.37 and guidance of $7.10-$7.50). 
  * F2Q27E(Dec-end) Guide: Expect revenue and earnings to track modestly ahead of consensus. We are forecasting revenue of $4.6 bn (vs. consensus of $4.5 bn), representing growth of +64% y/y. Meanwhile, we are forecasting gross margins of 59.5% (vs. consensus of 59.0%) and operating margins of 52.9% (vs. consensus of 52.8%), which leads to our earnings forecast of $8.68 (vs. consensus of $8.46).



## Western Digital (WDC)

### Product Transitions to Temper Near-Term Growth in FY27; Path to
Reacceleration to Be in Focus

Western Digital shares have declined -24% since the last earnings print (vs. a
+3% for S&P 500), as multiple product transitions weighed on F4Q26 exabyte
shipment growth, while implied F1Q27 guidance points to another quarter of
growth below both the company’s long-term target of 25%+ and its peer.
Nonetheless, underlying demand remains robust, with management indicating
industry demand growth slightly above this target, supported by rising data
requirements as AI expands from training into other applications. Against this
backdrop, we expect Western Digital to deliver F1Q27 (Sep-end) earnings better
than consensus, with guidance for F2Q27 (Dec-end) following a similar setup as
strong demand is balanced by the product transitions. Importantly, we expect
investors to focus on the trajectory of EB growth through the year,
particularly with expectations for the overhang to moderate in combination
with the introduction and ramp of HAMR products heading into CY27. Thus, we
are tweaking our model to reflect the aforementioned dynamics, while
maintaining our long-term expectations for 25%+ EB growth and leaving our out-
year earnings estimates largely unchanged. Similar to Seagate, given broader
investor scrutiny around uncertainty related to AI investment, as well as more
specific risks to the HDD industry in such an environment, particularly if
additional drive capacity were to come online, we are reducing our target
multiple to the mid-teens (vs. high-teens prior), such that our December 2027
price target now tracks to $600 (vs. $715 prior).

  * F1Q27 (Sep-end) Results: Earnings to track ahead of consensus. We are forecasting revenue of $4.2 bn (vs. consensus of $4.1 bn and guidance of $4.0-$4.2 bn), representing growth of +48% y/y. Meanwhile, we are forecasting gross margins of 56.5% (vs. consensus of 56% and guidance of 55-56%) and operating margins of 47% (vs. consensus of 46.4%), which leads to our earnings forecast of $4.17 (vs. consensus of $4.09 and guidance of $3.85-$4.15). 
  * F2Q27E(Dec-end) Guide: Expect revenue and earnings to track broadly in-line with consensus. We are forecasting revenue of $4.5 bn (vs. consensus of $4.6 bn), representing growth of +49% y/y. Meanwhile, we are forecasting gross margins of 58.5% (vs. consensus of 57.7%) and operating margins of 49.7% (vs. consensus of 48.6%), which leads to our earnings forecast of $4.80 (vs. consensus of $4.77). 



#

# Investment Thesis, Valuation and Risks

### Seagate (Overweight; Price Target: $1,050.00)

### Investment Thesis

We rate Seagate shares Overweight on account of a very attractive set up for
the overall HDD industry, which is positioned to benefit from both strong
demand stemming from hyperscaler capex plans as well as pricing tailwinds. STX
is ahead in terms of technology transition and is already shipping next-
generation HAMR based solutions to data center customers. Near- and medium-
term fundamentals continue to improve as the industry is being disciplined in
adding new capacity and focusing on profitable growth.

### Valuation

We are lowering our December 2027 price target to $1,050 (vs. $1,240 prior),
based on valuing our 2028E EPS estimate at a ~15x P/E multiple. We believe the
target multiple is justified as it is well ahead of the historical multiple
driven by robust demand from hyperscaler capex plans, and still conservative
relative to some other AI-levered vendors (e.g. Optical) to reflect less
aggressive pricing actions.

### Risks to Rating and Price Target

Downside risks to our rating and price target include a slowdown in Cloud
capex spending on AI infrastructure, which could present risk to demand growth
forecasts for the HDD industry despite the current robust pipeline of
investment announcements. Additionally, technology disruptions – including
faster-than-expected migration to flash-based storage driven by narrowing cost
differentials between HDDs and NAND, and greater progress on NAND density
could present headwinds to our expectations for Seagate shares.

# Investment Thesis, Valuation and Risks

### Western Digital (Overweight; Price Target: $600.00)

### Investment Thesis

We rate Western Digital shares Overweight driven primarily by the opportunity
for significant upside to consensus estimates, with the HDD industry
positioned to benefit from both strong demand stemming from hyperscaler capex
plans as well as pricing tailwinds. WDC is a powerhouse in storage, with its
portfolio comprising next-generation HDD solutions that are addressing the
growing data storage requirements at data center/cloud/AI infrastructure
customers. Near- and medium-term fundamentals continue to improve as the
industry is being disciplined in adding new capacity and focusing on
profitable growth.

### Valuation

We are lowering our December 2027 price target to $600 (vs. $715 prior), based
on valuing our 2028E EPS estimate at a ~15x P/E multiple, which is largely in-
line with the target multiple for the key peer Seagate- and is ahead of the
historical multiple given robust HDD storage demand across data centers.

**Alphabet** {Ticker: **GOOG.OQ** , Closing Price: **336.91 USD** , Target
Price: **430.0 USD** , Recommendation: **Buy**}  
  
Click here for the
Model  
  
Our channel checks (link and
link to our recent notes)
suggest **Search revenue growth remains relatively healthy** , driven largely
by higher pricing, incremental AIO ad revenue, and a gradual decline in the
efficacy of SEO, which has supported auction dynamics in paid channels. On the
back of these trends, we think the buyside is broadly in line with Street
estimates for 14% y/y FXN Search growth of the 3Q, implying 190bps
deceleration in y/y growth given the more challenging y/y compares. Our data
checks suggest steady growth across desktop/mobile web visits (see figure 1 in
note), as well as consistent to improving growth across Chrome/ Google App
DAUs and sessions per user (see figure 2 in note). These data checks suggest
that aggregate search volume remains robust in our view. Similarly, our intra-
quarter checks on GCP suggest yet another quarter of acceleration, with Google
seemingly benefiting from more available capacity vs peers. As such, both NTM
commitments and consumption growth accelerated from June to September. On the
back of these favorable checks, in addition to growing contribution from TPU
direct sales this quarter, our conversations with investors appears to suggest
GCP growth to surpass 100% this quarter (we are at 92% FXN in the 3Q, modestly
above consensus). In fact, our checks suggest GCP is increasingly becoming a
second platform for production workloads among ISV and Digital Native
customers and also capturing a growing share of spend from AI Natives amid
constraints elsewhere.That said, the narrative for Alphabet has been less
constructive over the last few weeks with the emergence of several new
competitive model launches (Meta's Muse Wonder being the latest) and the quick
adoption of personal digital agents including Meta’s Muse as well Spear Street
Technology’s Instinct. As adoption of these agents expands, the risk is that
commercial requests are directed via agents and not Google Search which could
have a negative impact on Search paid click growth over time. We believe that
Google should be a leading contender within consumer agents: it has access to
Gmail, user’s search queries, map data, the company controls Android, has
existing merchant relationships etc. , which in theory should provide some of
the key foundational pillars to launch a successful personal agent. In
addition, the company is an infrastructure leader and the early benchmarks for
Gemini 4 appear promising. As such, we do expect the focus of the call to
center around Google’s potential consumer agentic response, and we anticipate
questions around the potential additive / cannibalistic nature of agents
relative to the Search business and whether or not the company has adequate
capacity to both accelerate the GCP business while simultaneously offer a
horizontal agent with broad consumer appeal. Zooming out, we still view GOOG
as a structural winner across advertising, Cloud, and AI infrastructure. AI
appears to be expanding Search usage and monetizable intent, while Cloud’s
scale and Alphabet’s integrated stack across TPUs, models, software, and
distribution create an increasingly meaningful second earnings engine. Direct
TPU sales add another growth channel, with Waymo providing longer-term
optionality. **Higher capital intensity remains a concern, but we contend that
Alphabet is investing against visible demand that continues to exceed supply
and remains adequately funded following its recent equity and debt raises.**
We maintain GOOG as a top pick for 2026 and retain our $430 price target,
based on 29x our marginally higher FY27 GAAP EPS estimate.**Our ad checks have
been mostly inline****Our three recent ad checks point to healthy but uneven
Search trends** (for more please see
here and
here). Two checks highlighted
growth accelerating modestly through 3Q26, while the third saw a roughly
300bps deceleration that was largely related to tougher y/y comps. That said,
underlying indicators remained constructive, with paid-click and conversion
growth improving, while AI Overviews, AI Mode, and zero-click results are
reducing organic referrals and pushing advertisers toward paid acquisition.
Overall, we think the checks support current Street estimates, although
tougher comparisons and macro exposure likely limit near-term upside. On the
back of these checks, we modestly trim our 3Q Search revenue estimates to
$64.7bn from $65.4bn, up 14.3% y/y (and up 13.5% y/y FXN), which is now in
line with Street estimates.**YouTube trends appeared considerably stronger** ,
with one check showing spend growth accelerating ~400bps to the high teens in
3Q26 and another 170bps step-up expected in 4Q. The top-line strength appears
to be benefiting from an increase in ad load (+8% according to one expert),
fewer skippable ads, more professional content, and political spending that
has more than doubled versus the prior midterm cycle. While event-driven
spending provided a meaningful tailwind, the checks suggest YouTube is
outperforming current expectations and taking a larger share of digital video
budgets. All in, we are therefore modestly raising our estimate for YouTube
revenue by 60bps to $11.6bn, up 13.3% y/y (and 12.5% y/y FXN), and above the
Street at $11.4bn.**Cloud checks have been positive** GCP trends strengthened
further in 3Q, with NTM committed-dollar growth accelerating to 48.5% in
September from 45% in June with consumption growth also increasing to just
over 48% from 45%. According to our check, Google appeared better positioned
than peers on near-term capacity, in part because the company has been able
reallocate infrastructure from other parts of the business to Cloud, allowing
commitments to convert into consumption within weeks rather than waiting for
new data centers. This capacity advantage is helping GCP become a second
production platform for more ISVs and digital-native customers while capturing
incremental AI-native demand displaced by constraints elsewhere. Adoption of
Google’s custom silicon is also broadening, with Ironwood TPUs now sold
directly and deployed across several GCP customer and neocloud environments.
Overall, we contend that the checks point to sustained share gains, tighter
alignment between bookings and revenue, and an expanding monetization
opportunity across both Cloud services and AI infrastructure. All in, we now
expect Google Cloud revenue of $29.2bn, up 93% y/y, modestly above consensus
at $28.8bn. In aggregate, we expect total revenue to grow ~24% y/y FXN in the
3Q, marginally above the Street, and modestly accelerating versus 2Q26 despite
a ~140bps tougher comp. We are also projecting GAAP OI of $43.9bn, or 34.3%
margins up ~380ps y/y and ~30bps q/q. A key investor question since Meta
launched Muse has been when will Google introduce a comparable consumer agent.
We believe Google has the assets to build a differentiated offering: Search
captures user intent; Gmail, YouTube, Maps, Google Pay, and Android provide
broad context on user activity; and the company already has deep relationships
with advertisers and retailers. As such, it appears to us to be a question of
“when” not “if”. That said, the longer Meta’s head start, the more opportunity
Muse has to accumulate user context, deepen engagement, and secure
permissions, potentially increasing switching friction over time.Looking
beyond the potential launch of an agent, investors also appear focused on two
further potential risks: Search cannibalization and capacity allocation. On
Search, agentic workflows could reduce traditional query volumes. That said,
AI Overviews and AI Mode are already reducing organic referrals, which has
increased businesses’ reliance on paid Search. Moreover, Google’s advertiser
relationships, merchant integrations, and understanding of commercial intent
should allow it to monetize transactions across agentic interfaces
(potentially expanding the TAM). As such, we continue to believe that Google
remains well positioned to capture the underlying commercial value driven by a
personal agent (once launched).On the capacity side, compute and memory
allocated to a consumer agent with a longer monetization curve could
potentially generate near-term GCP revenue. However, we note that GCP is
accelerating even at scale; our checks suggest that Google appears to have
more near-term capacity flexibility than peers, and continued infrastructure
investment should expand the available resource pool over time. We therefore
contend that any opportunity cost likely moderates as more capacity comes
online, while the strategic value of controlling the consumer-agent layer
could compound over a much longer period.Looking further out to 2027, another
topic that comes up in our investor conversations is TPU sales, which fall
under two different buckets: outright chip sales that could include ~3.5GW of
capacity to a Blackstone JV with a frontier lab (starting in 2027) and leasing
of additional capacity on GCP itself. Consensus is projecting ~10GW of chip
capacity by Broadcom in 2027, of which we think about 8GW may be TPUs. If we
assume 2GW of these chips are sold to the JV at $20-$25bn/GW, that would
amount to ~$40-$50bn in chip sales for Google. The remaining 6GW of capacity
could add another $60-$90bn of annualized revenue in 2027 assuming
$10-$15bn/GW per year. In aggregate, we think TPUs could represent an
additional $80-$100bn of revenue in 2027.Importantly, in our view, Alphabet
now has three durable growth engines: advertising, Cloud services, and AI
hardware, with Waymo providing an additional longer-term option. We believe
this improving mix can support durable growth and a higher valuation as
investors increasingly recognize Alphabet as an AI infrastructure and platform
company rather than primarily an advertising business.  We maintain our Buy
rating and price target of $430,  which is based off 29x our FY27 GAAP EPS
estimate._For more details and our expectations, please click below_

OCP Takeaways: The event offered relatively little new information, in our
view, with presentations largely providing additional color on existing
architectures and confirming previously disclosed roadmaps. Across the
numerous presentations, we saw a focus on solutions to power constraints,
evolving optical architectures, and broader industry alignment around the
infrastructure needed to scale AI. While we come away from the event generally
neutral, it's clear that the supply chain is coming together to support the
continued proliferation of AI, from hyperscalers and industrial players to
semiconductor companies.

800 VDC Data Center: Native 800 VDC rack delivery was confirmed as shifting
toward the Feynman generation in 2028, as we'd expected in our preview
heading into
OCP.
In addition to broader presentations from supply chain partners, NVIDIA
reiterated the phased transition, with power sidecars shipping now,
centralized power centers targeted for deployment in 2027, and native 800 VDC
rack delivery aligned with the Feynman generation in 2028. As such, we
reiterate our view that the 800 VDC adoption curve isn't stopping, but will be
a smoother and more gradual curve vs the significant inflection initially
expected next year.

We also saw demos from several power semiconductor/analog companies on the
show floor supporting NVIDIA's MGX architecture, though we'd caution against
interpreting participation as a "winner's circle." Rather, we view these
demonstrations as evidence of ecosystem participation and technical
validation, which is separate from securing specific production design wins.
Some demos focused on intermediate bus converters (IBCs) and hot-swap
solutions, representing different opportunities across the power tree, with
GaN increasingly relevant for high-density DC/DC conversion. We continue to
see a meaningful opportunity for power semis as rack densities increase, but
favor those in our coverage with more exposure toward front-end conversion and
point-of-load power delivery.

Land, Power, Shell: A common thread throughout the presentations was the focus
on solutions to the land, power and shell constraints facing hyperscalers and
data center operators. These ranged from 800 VDC power architectures designed
to improve efficiency and reduce power losses across the data center, to
energy storage systems that smooth rapid power fluctuations and reduce the
need to size infrastructure for peak demand.

NVIDIA highlighted two approaches to improving power utilization: MaxLPS
(Maximum Land, Power, Shell), a suite of hardware and software technologies
within its DSX AI factory platform, which dynamically allocates power across
GPUs and racks to enable more compute within the same facility power budget;
and Intelligent Power Smoothing (IPS), which combines energy storage and GPU-
level controls to smooth rapid power fluctuations and reduce peak power
requirements. Both aim to make better use of available power capacity,
allowing data center operators to scale compute without requiring a
proportional increase in power infrastructure.

We think this is a key point, as hyperscalers wrestle with land/power/shell
shortages, that we should not underestimate the industry's ability to adapt
and optimize around these limitations, as we have basically seen throughout
this AI cycle.

Memory: Again most of the memory conversations were in in line with our
thinking, but it did seem noteworthy that Hynix (covered by Shawn Kim) spent a
significant portion of its talk on high bandwidth flash, saying that it can
provide about half of the HBM bandwidth but 14x higher capacity. This could
become significant upside optionality for Sandisk, who has also put strong
emphasis on the standard.

Optical insights: We'll let our optical expert Meta Marshall do the real
analysis here but to us it felt status quo. There does appear to be
significant emphasis on cost reduction technologies such as LPO or active
copper, which is not new, while NVIDIA continues to be most convicted on CPO
for scale-out. We expect to get significantly more attention on this at the
NVIDIA GTC Berlin event, which we are also attending.

\----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Reiterating our AMD views: Last week, our Asia team, led by Howard Kao,
received significant media attention for cutting its AMD substrate forecast.
This appeared to be more of a housekeeping adjustment, albeit a large one, to
a number that we have zero ability to triangulate to AMD shipments. This was a
separate, independent change published as part of a much larger note, and we
do not believe it is impactful to our forecasts.
